title: ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’: A New Wave of Consumer Debt
summary: NYT Daily podcast episode on BNPL's growth into everyday essentials and one user's cycle of dependence on the loans.

assertions.quote: I signed up with a firm. Five minutes later, I had a $6,000 credit line
about half the people who use buy now, pay later loans say they couldn't make the purchase without them
Flex... do about $2 billion a month in rent loans... expanding into utilities and auto loans

verdicts.note: Providers including Affirm and Flex have launched rent- and bill-financing products, and survey data shows rising use for necessities.
LendingTree: 13% of BNPL users have used the loans to pay rent, and grocery use has more than doubled over two years (14% to 29%).

assertions.quote: there's only two places for these companies to make their money. It's the merchants or the consumers
every lender is kind of making their own decisions in lending you money
Americans spend about 3 trillion a year on credit cards... buy now, pay later is about 160 billion
harm reduction... it's just not a good sign about where we're at with the affordability crisis

verdicts.note: A reasonable reading of usage data, but distinguishing 'preference' from 'desperation' as the driver is inherently interpretive.
LendingTree: 54% of BNPL users say they wouldn't be able to make ends meet without the loans, alongside rising grocery use -- consistent with a necessity-driven, affordability-stress narrative.

CFPB cites an Australian regulator finding that 20% of surveyed BNPL users cut back on or went without essentials (e.g., meals) to make BNPL payments on time and 15% took out an additional loan to do so, plus a separate US survey finding 32% had to delay or skip an essential bill because of BNPL payments -- evidence of financial strain consistent with an affordability-crisis reading.
